description: arXiv:2604.18572v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis posits that neural networks trained on different modalities (e.g., text and images) converge toward a shared representation of reality. If true, this has significant implications for whether modality choice matters at all. In this paper, we show that the evidence for this claim is substantially weak...
